### ASSISTANT [2026-06-10T02:50:31]
## Decision 1 — the precision/megakernel conflict, in full

**The collision.** Two of your standing decisions intersect badly:
- *Race precision*: industry-standard **bf16** mixed precision (your call after the fp8/int8 study) — matmuls/activations run bf16 under autocast, fp32 master weights and optimizer math.
- *Megakernels*: the L3-real cells (decoder/vit/mamba × adamw, soon more) compute **everything in fp32** — they were built fp32-first so parity vs the fp64 oracle is provable at ~1e-7 (which is also exactly how we caught the stride bug).

The race metric is steps-to-grok, and precision *changes grokking trajectories* (bf16's rounding noise acts as a small regularizer; the precision study measured different step counts per precision). So if decoder×adamw trains inside the fp32 megakernel while lion and the other nine race in eager bf16, AdamW's number is confounded — it's a precision difference wearing an optimizer-difference costume. Same model, same batch, *different arithmetic*. That violates the same fairness principle as your identical-batch-size rule. Hence the gate I'm adding: L3 runs only when the run's resolved precision is fp32.

**Your three real options:**

**A. bf16-retrofit the kernels** (~2-3 days). Implement bf16 compute in the stage headers (bf16 storage/matmuls, fp32 accumulators, fp32 optimizer tail — mirroring autocast semantics). The megakernels then ARE the race vehicle at your chosen precision, the roofline numbers describe the actual race, and ViT/Mamba smem footprints halve (188→~95KB, 145→~73KB). The catch: I have to match torch autocast's op-level dtype policy exactly (autocast keeps softmax/layernorm/CE in fp32 — if my precision boundaries differ from eager's, we've re-created the comparability problem one level down), and all parity gates need bf16-calibrated tolerances. Real, careful work; delays the race by those days.

**B. Race on eager bf16; megakernels stay the fp32 validation/roofline showcase** (zero extra work). Race starts as soon as tuning converges. The megakernels remain fully validated artifacts with their own benchmark section — launch-elimination and roofline gains demonstrated at fp32 — but the headline race numbers come from the eager path. Honest, faster, slightly weaker portfolio punchline ("built it, proved it, raced beside it").

**C. Race everything at fp32** (zero extra work, different trade). Set the race to fp32: every cell same arithmetic, and the megakernel cells run fused *in* the race — consistency preserved because L3-fp32 ≡ eager-fp32 (proven to the chaos floor). Worth knowing: **the grokking literature is canonically full-precision** — bf16 is the industry standard for *large-scale training*, not for grokking experiments. And your earlier per-model auto-precision had vit/mamba at fp32 anyway. Cost: fp32 matmuls are ~2× slower than bf16 → longer race wall-clock, and it walks back the "industry standard" call.

My read: **C** if you want megakernels in the race *now* and scientific conventionality; **A** if the few days are acceptable for the strongest engineering story; **B** if race speed dominates everything.

## Decision 3 — the six orphaned `models.*` bindings

`bindings.cpp` exports a `models` pybind submodule: `decoder_attention_forward/backward`, `vit_attention_forward/backward`, `mamba_selective_scan_forward/backward`. The cleanup sweep found **zero callers anywhere** — not the race, not the tuner, not one test. They're scaffolding from the earlier per-op model-kernel phase, superseded by the megakernel architecture.

The fork:
- **Delete the exports** (my recommendation). Your portability directive — "components individually portable into other projects" — is satisfied by the *stage headers* under `csrc/fused/` + `COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md`; that's the designed reuse surface. An exported-but-untested-and-unused Python API is pure portfolio liability: a reviewer who calls one and hits a rough edge has found a bug in dead code. Deleting costs nothing; the device code stays recoverable in git and the headers carry the real capability.
- **Keep as a deliberate public API** — "call fused attention primitives from Python" as a product feature. Then they need what they currently lack: tests, docs, and parity coverage (~half a day), otherwise they're advertised functionality that's silently unvalidated — the exact pattern we've been hunting all week.

## Decision 2 — locked in as you specified

Early termination **only** on grokking (val ≥ 0.95, test-confirmed at stop — already the stopper's design). No heuristic "hopeless-run" auto-kill: cells that don't grok run to the 20k cap and get recorded as honest DNFs. I supervise the race live — monitors on the runner; any crash, NaN, stall, or anomaly and I go in, diagnose, fix, and rerun that cell rather than letting automation paper over it. One consequence to know: DNF-heavy cells consume their full cap, so the wall-clock estimate's upper range applies to however many cells fail to grok — I'll give you the calibrated ETA from real per-cell step rates before launch.

### ASSISTANT [2026-06-10T02:58:58]
On the roofline point — yes, it's standing requirement #4, but let me be precise about where the megakernels actually stand, because "close to the ceiling" has two very different parts here:

## Honest current state: they're launch-optimal, not FLOP-optimal

The L3 cells as built are **correctness-first**: scalar owner-computes matmuls, fp32, samples processed one-at-a-time per CTA (the agents documented this trade explicitly — SG2's tensor-per-CTA even idles ~100 CTAs on small tensors). Zero tensor-core usage today. Their first-order win is eliminating the *launch-bound regime*: the eager step is dozens of kernel launches whose latency dwarfs this workload's actual math (~1-2 GFLOP/step ≈ single-digit µs of pure bf16 compute on an H100). The megakernel moves the bottleneck from launch latency to real compute/memory — which is precisely what makes your roofline metric *meaningful* for them. But measured against the compute roof right now, they'd sit far below it.

## The fix is already your decision A — the bf16 retrofit IS the roofline program

One program, not two passes over the kernels:

1. **bf16 compute + fp32 accumulators** — 2× arithmetic density, halves the smem working sets (ViT 188→~95 KB, Mamba 145→~73 KB → occupancy headroom).
2. **Tensor-core MMA for the stage GEMMs** — the big multiplier. The model shapes are MMA-friendly (d=128: in_proj 384×128, ff 512×128, attention head tiles), and replacing the scalar loops with `mma.sync` tiles is what actually climbs toward the bf16 roof (989 TF/s dense peak) instead of the SIMT fp32 roof (~67).
3. **Warp-per-sample batch parallelism** inside each CTA (the flagged follow-up in all three specs) — sample-serial CTAs can't hide latency; this raises arithmetic intensity per SM.
4. **SG2: sequence-space partitioning** across CTAs (the design-req-#1 layout the agent documented as the perf follow-up) instead of tensor-per-CTA.

Here's the full playbook, ranked by multiplier, with the physics quantified first so the targets are honest.

## Why we're far today (the gap, in numbers)

Decoder cell, full batch (~4.7k samples × seq 4 ≈ 18.8k tokens): fwd+bwd ≈ **~45 GFLOP/step**. At the H100's bf16 tensor-core roof (989 TF/s) that's **~45 µs of pure math**. We currently take ~80 ms/step — so the step runs at **~0.05% of the compute roof**. The megakernel already killed the launch overhead; what remains is that the kernel does its math as *scalar fp32 loops over one sample at a time* — seq=4 rows per GEMM is no arithmetic intensity at all — and it round-trips **~446 MB/step** of per-CTA gradient partials through HBM (132 CTAs × 422k floats, written then re-read for reduction).

So the distance to the roof is three stacked problems: no tensor cores, no batch tiling, and a fat reduction. The levers, biggest first:

## 1. Batch-tiled tensor-core GEMMs (the 100×-class lever)
Restructure P1 from "each CTA loops its samples through tiny per-sample GEMMs" to **layer-by-layer batched GEMMs over the whole token dimension**: activations live as [18.8k × 128] tiles, every matmul becomes `wgmma` (sm_90's async warpgroup MMA — the codebase already carries `wgs::` warpgroup primitives) with M=18.8k to tile against. All the shapes are MMA-clean (in_proj 384×128, ff 512×128, out_proj 128×128, head 97→pad 112×128; K=128 = 8×k16). This is writing a mini-CUTLASS pipeline inside the persistent kernel — it's the real work in decision A, and it's what moves us from "launch-optimal" to "compute-meaningful."

## 2. Kill the partial-grad round-trip via split-K ownership (the memory lever)
The weight-grad is `dW = Xᵀ @ dY` with K = 18.8k tokens — perfect for **tile ownership**: each CTA owns a dW tile and contracts over the full batch itself. The 446 MB/step of per-CTA partials *disappears entirely* (no partial buffers, no P2 reduction pass), the reduction becomes tensor-core math, and determinism is preserved by construction (fixed tile ownership, fixed k-order, still zero float atomics).

## 3. Optimizer-in-epilogue fusion
Once dW tiles finish in registers, apply AdamW/Lion *right there* in the GEMM epilogue — m/v update + weight write while the tile is register-resident. Eliminates one full grad write + read. The optimizer tail is already bandwidth-bound and vec4-clean; this removes its memory pass almost completely.

## 4. TMA + producer/consumer warpgroup pipeline
`cp.async.bulk`/TMA staging of activation and weight tiles, double-buffered, with producer warps feeding consumer warpgroups (`setmaxnreg` rebalancing — the FlashAttention-3 pattern). This is what keeps the wgmma units fed so #1's peak is actually reachable rather than theoretical.

## 5. bf16 storage everywhere (already decided)
Halves all activation/weight traffic and smem (ViT 188→~95 KB, Mamba 145→~73 KB), doubles effective cache. fp32 accumulators throughout — which, note, matches eager autocast's numerics *class* better than today's all-fp32 does, so the bf16 parity gates (chaos-floor methodology) get easier, not harder.

## 6. Per-model specifics
- **Mamba**: the scan is elementwise-recurrent — memory-roof-bound, not TC-bound; it's already register-resident (correct design). Its GEMMs (in/x/dt/out_proj) join the tiled pipeline; the scan's roof is HBM bandwidth and it's close already.
- **SG2 tail**: sequence-space partitioning across CTAs (the documented follow-up) instead of tensor-per-CTA (~100 idle CTAs today), plus the in-CTA bitonic sort to delete the one remaining host round-trip.
- **Grid barriers**: ~2-5 µs each; with steps shrinking to ~100 µs they start to matter — collapse stages where the split-K design makes barriers unnecessary (it removes the P1→P2 barrier outright).

## 7. Make the autotuner own the new dims
Tile shapes, pipeline stages, warpgroup counts, samples-per-CTA — all become tunable dimensions through the existing `_kernel_tuned.json` machinery, so the roofline distance gets *searched*, not hand-guessed.

## Projected end-state (honest)
Hand persistent kernels on these shapes realistically land **20-40% of the TC roof on the GEMM phases**, with the step floor set by the elementwise/optimizer memory traffic (~10-20 µs at 3.35 TB/s) plus a few barriers. That's a step time of **~100-300 µs vs today's ~80 ms — a 250-800× step-rate improvement**, which would turn 20k-step race cells into ~minutes and make the roofline plot genuinely impressive rather than apologetic. I'd phase it: **R1** (days): warp-per-sample + bf16 + split-K reduction → ~5-15×; **R2** (the core, ~week): wgmma+TMA tiled pipeline + epilogue fusion → the big jump; **R3**: SG2/Mamba specializations. Every phase passes the same gates: parity vs eager-bf16 at calibrated tolerances, determinism (fixed ownership, no atomics), then quiet-GPU roofline measurement per cell, SASS-audited (wgmma/TMA actually present in the binary, not assumed).

One framing decision for you when R2 lands: the race's *step-rate* story changes so dramatically that we should re-calibrate the race ETA then — the serialized full sweep may drop from days to hours.

**Why not now.** The R2 retrofit is about to reshape the sm_90 model-stage headers (scalar loops → tiled wgmma/TMA pipelines). Bringing up mi300x against today's scalar design means doing the port twice. Let the sm_90 R2 design settle first — it becomes the template the MFMA port follows.

**Why race-launch is the perfect boundary.** Your decision 2 makes the race a supervision job for me, not an editing job — days of wall time where the H100 is busy and my hands are free. And the race imposes a freeze anyway: nothing it imports may change mid-race or the results are invalidated. I'll enforce that mechanically — **the race runs from a pinned git checkout**, not the live tree. That single move is most of your contamination answer: the racing code is physically immutable while mi300x work proceeds.

**The full protection stack** (now in durable memory):
1. **Directory isolation by design** — gfx942 work lives in `csrc/fused/gfx942/`, `kernels/gfx942/`, per-arch substrate; it *cannot* touch sm_90 binaries. The 33 `.hip` cells already exist from the pre-silicon emit, waiting.
2. **Branch discipline** — gfx942 bring-up on its own branch; merges only after the full H100 gate battery re-passes on the merge candidate.
3. **Canonical math frozen** — `csrc/algorithms/*.h` is the shared single source. During bring-up, gfx942 adapts *to* it, never the reverse; `check_math_single_source.py` already enforces this arch-agnostically.
4. **The validation ladder transfers** — the fp64 oracles and structural mirrors are CPU/arch-independent and already green; mi300x needs only its own silicon gates (parity gate, megakernel-vs-eager, grok smokes), which the harness already parameterizes by arch. And expect them to catch real bugs — every silicon so far has (inverted wd, stride bugs, the `_RET` loop). "Compile-verified" gfx942 will be no different; that's what the gates are for.

**Two GPUs at once** — yes, workable either way: same box (CUDA and ROCm toolchains coexist; separate device visibility) or separate machine (separate session, coordination through git, which the branch discipline handles). The agent fan-out pattern extends naturally: mi300x build/gate agents run there while I supervise the race here.

**On routine cleanups** — locked in as standing requirement #7: a dead-code/bug/optimization sweep after every major phase (integration landing, retrofit, race milestones), not a one-time pass. The next one fires right after the current integration + rebuild gate cycle.

So: provision it whenever convenient — it can sit idle — but I'll start writing gfx942 code the day the H100 race starts from its pinned checkout. ### SECTION 5 — Dim registry → winner → flag plumbing, and the 7-new-wgmma-dims seam

**This is the highest-value finding. There is a SILENT-DROP trap on the canonical product path.**

How winners map dim→flag today (in range):
- `_write_tuned_configs_header` (14040) builds `name_to_macro = {d["name"]: d["macro"] for d in dims}` from `load_embedded_search_space()` (14083) and emits `#ifndef/#define` per dim → writes `tuned_configs.h` (the **secondary** consumer, 14067/14491).
- `build_jit` (14503–14506) calls `_variant_macros(tuned, dims, "host"/"device", …)` to turn winning dims into `-D&lt;MACRO&gt;=val` on the **final rebuild** line.
- `_export_kernel_tuned_json` (13994) → `inject.export_winner` writes `_kernel_tuned.json` — the **canonical** handoff setup.py bakes into the shipped `_ops.so`.

**The trap (docstring 14001–14002, explicit):** `_export_kernel_tuned_json` persists **ONLY the 5 SAFE per-TU dims** (block / vec / unroll / async_depth + maxrregcount); "everything else in `combo` is dropped." So if you add 7 wgmma dims (`SG_TUNED_TILE_N`, pipeline depth, warpgroup count, samples-per-CTA, cluster size, swizzle, etc.), the autotuner will tune them, time them, pick a winner, and write them to `tuned_configs.h` — but they are **silently dropped from `_kernel_tuned.json` and never reach the shipped `_ops.so`.** This is a textbook "looks-done-but-not-wired" landmine: the secondary consumer shows the right values; the product build ships in-header defaults.

**End-to-end seam to add 7 new wgmma dims (ordered; bottleneck flagged):**
1. **[out of range]** Add each dim to the per-arch builder (`_sm90_full_space` etc., ~9843 ArchEntry wiring) with `name`, `values`, `macro` (e.g. `SG_TUNED_TILE_N`), and `applies_to`/`target`. Mark `live: True` so it's not pinned/collapsed (`_is_dead_dim`; `test_dead_dims_pinned_and_collapsed` 16492) and ensure it enters `config_key` (else two distinct configs collapse).
2. **[in range, AUTOMATIC]** `_write_tuned_configs_header`'s `name_to_macro` (14083) and `_variant_macros` (14503) pick up any dim carrying a `macro` automatically — header + final-rebuild flags need **no edit**. ✔
3. **[THE BOTTLENECK — out of range, must edit]** Expand the SAFE allowlist in `_tuned_inject.MACROS` / `export_winner` (referenced at 14084–14085 as kept "in lockstep") so the new macros are persisted to `_kernel_tuned.json`. **Without this single change, steps 1/2 produce a green tune that ships nothing.** Make this the headline of any wgmma-dim work.
4. **[in range, must keep in lockstep]** Update the two back-compat dim→macro maps that exist as failure fallbacks: `_write_tuned_configs_header` backcompat (14089–14094) and the `build_jit` except-path map (14512–14514). On a healthy space-load these are redundant; on a failed load they're the only macros emitted, so a new SAFE dim must be added here too or it vanishes on the degraded path.
5. **[out of range]** setup.py reads `_kernel_tuned.json` → `-DSG_TUNED_TILE_N=…` per AUTOTUNE_LINKAGE.md (automatic once step 3 lands).
6. **[meta]** If a new dim introduces a plumbing function, add it to the `FEATURES` allowlist (18840) or `test_mandate_features_have_nontest_callsites` won't guard it.

So the dim→header→flag path is pleasingly automatic (steps 2/4), but the dim→**product** path has a hard manual gate at step 3 that's easy to miss and fails *silently*. Recommendation: make `export_winner` persist any dim that carries a `macro` (deriving the allowlist from the live search space) instead of a hand-maintained SAFE set — that would make the wgmma-dim landing truly end-to-end and kill the silent-drop class.

## THE MAMBA BLOCKER (headline finding — needs sign-off)
**Root cause: a forward-pass smem row-stride mismatch in the directive-frozen `csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_mamba3.cuh`** (the recurrence of the exact bug class that commit 5cb32b8 fixed elsewhere; that commit "audited mamba clean" but mamba was **never GPU-run** — my evidence disproves the freeze's premise).

**Exact location:** `mb_forward_sample`, the per-layer output path:
- Line 699 writes `r` into `sm-&gt;adj_c[s][o]` where `adj_c` is `float[kSeq][kDInner]` (= `[8][256]`), so row stride **256**.
- Line 704 passes `&amp;sm-&gt;adj_c[0][0]` to `mb_layernorm_fwd`, which (line 330) reads `x + s*mb::kD` — row stride **128**.
- For row s≥1 the LayerNorm reads flat `s*128` but the data is at `s*256`, reading uninitialized smem.

**Evidence (conclusive, seam exonerated):**
- A standalone harness (`_mamba_fwd_probe.cu`, since removed) that includes `model_stage_mamba3.cuh` and calls `mb_forward_sample` directly — **bypassing my entire seam** — reproduces the bug. So dispatch routing, int-packing, `mb_bind`, P1/P2/P3, and the launcher are all exonerated.
- Field-by-field vs oracle: layer-0 forward is **bit-correct through `y_scan`** (`x_main_raw, conv, dt_pre, Bmat, Cmat, y_scan` all ~3e-7), then `ln_xhat` diverges.
- Row-level: layer-0 `ln_xhat` **row 0 = 8.8e-8 (correct), rows 1-7 = ~1.0-1.5 (garbage)** — the stride-mismatch signature.
- B=1 single-`mb_forward_sample` loss **jitters across processes** (5.09, 5.13, 5.06, 4.66) → uninitialized read, deterministic-within-process.

**Recommended fix (NOT applied — frozen file, appears sibling-owned):** add an input-row-stride parameter to `mb_layernorm_fwd` (pass `kDInner` at the layer call site), exactly the `ld*` pattern commit 5cb32b8 used for `dec_linear_bwd`/`vit_linear_bwd`. Authorize the stage-header owner to apply it.

**Two caveats so this isn't mistaken for a one-line-and-green fix:**
- **Backward + P2/P3 are unverified by necessity** — all grads are garbage because the backward consumes corrupted forward caches, so I cannot distinguish "backward correct, fed garbage" from "backward also buggy." After the LN-stride fix re-greens the forward, the mamba gates must be re-run; further issues may surface.
- I found the **first-divergence** bug, not a full audit. Recommend a **full stride audit of `model_stage_mamba3.cuh`** (the 5cb32b8 "~70 seams" audit demonstrably missed this one).

I left the mamba GPU gates as raw-FAIL (most honest signal; not weakening — no kernel error is hidden). The seam is in clean final state (no smem-zeroing, no register hacks — I tried both as diagnostics and reverted; neither was the cause).

## ViT trajectory calibration (documented deviation — milder sign-off)
The spec-author's ViT-D gate was raw `max_loss_dev &lt; 1e-3` on the asymmetric loss across all 200 steps. This is **provably impossible** on ViT's stiff (wd=1.0) surface: a measured eager-vs-eager **1e-7 perturbation** on one tensor diverges to symmetric **27.5 / asymmetric 0.96** at the memorization cliff (~step 167), the SAME magnitude as fused-vs-eager (symmetric 29.4). I calibrated to the decoder's documented "two correct fp32 implementations separate chaotically" logic, with a denominator-robust metric and per-band measured-control bounds (3× control), keeping a SHARP pre-cliff gate (the real correctness check). **There is no decoder precedent for loosening a loss-trajectory gate** (the decoder kept its loss gate sharp, calibrated only final-params) — so this is a documented deviation needing sign-off. The constants (27.5, 0.876, 0.436) are seed-specific, like the decoder's 2e-2. Justification is the measured 1-ulp control; the keystone single-step gate (grads 2e-7) independently proves per-step correctness.

# Codebase-Wide `SG_TUNED_*` Registration Plan

## How registration actually works (the mechanism, verified)

Liveness is **auto-derived**, not hand-listed. `_kernel_source_macros()` (compile.py:1277) greps `csrc/` + `kernels/` for the regex `SG_TUNED_[A-Z0-9_]+`; `_is_dead_dim()` (L1310) marks a macro dim **live iff that exact token (or `TOKEN_*`) appears in source**. Consequences that drive every row below:

- **Registering a `_dim()` whose token is NOT in source is worse than a no-op**: `_is_dead_dim`→dead → `_pin_dead_dims` (L1393) truncates its values to one and drops it from `config_key`. Silently inert.
- A registered macro dim **IS swept** on the JIT side: `resolve_macros()` (compile.py:2707) emits `-D&lt;macro&gt;=&lt;val&gt;` generically for any dim with a `macro` field. **But it is only baked into the shipped `_ops*.so`** if its key is in `_tuned_inject.py::MACROS` (currently the 5 phase-1 keys only). Verified: `cluster_shape` is consumed+registered+live yet absent from `MACROS`, so its winner is timed but never shipped (AUTOTUNE_LINKAGE.md confirms "cluster_shape … phase-2 … not emitted").

**Therefore the recipe has up to 6 spots, and constant types are asymmetric:**

| Spot | File:loc | When needed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `_sm90_full_space` (compile.py:1798) / `_gfx942_full_space` (1892) — add `_dim(...)` | always (the registration) |
| 2 | `_DEAD_KEY_DIMS` — **derived** by `_dead_key_dims()` (1358); no manual edit | auto, *if* the token is in source |
| 3 | `megakernel_cell_search_space` (2193) — only special-cases `maxrregcount`; new dims flow through | auto |
| 4 | `_COST_MODEL_CANONICAL_DIM_VALUES` (4515) — add for one-hot featurization | optional; changes `FEATURE_DIM` → invalidates saved `cost_model_*.bin` |
| 5 | `_LIVE_TUNING_DIMS` (1263) — defensive floor | hygiene only; load-bearing **only** when source scan is empty (bodyless wheel) |
| **6** | **`_tuned_inject.py`: `MACROS` + `_EMIT_ORDER` + `_PERSIST_KEYS`** | **required to SHIP the winner into `.so`** (else swept-live only) |

**Constant types:**
- **Type A** — `#ifndef SG_TUNED_X` guard already present, dim missing → register (spots 1,4,6); immediately live. *(Only the 6 R2-header macros are pure Type A.)*
- **Type A′ (wrong-prefix)** — `#ifndef`-guarded but under a non-`SG_TUNED_` token (`SG2_MEGA_BLOCK`, `SG_&lt;OPT&gt;_MIN_BLOCKS`). Invisible to the auto-derive scan. Prerequisite = **rename the existing guard token to `SG_TUNED_*`** (a source edit, cheaper than pure-hardcoded since the guard structure exists) + register.
- **Type B** — hardcoded literal, no guard → prerequisite = **add `#ifndef SG_TUNED_X` guard + consume it** (a source edit, outside this edit-nothing scope) + register.

RISKY = changes reduction order / smem layout / thread count → re-run `tests/hw/parity_gate_h100.py` + `tests/hw/test_reference_parity.py` after the sweep. SAFE = ptxas-only (register cap / minBlocksPerSM) — no parity re-run.

## Per-arch sweep cost (TPE, not grid — build-dominated)

Sweep mechanics: Optuna TPE, optimizers run **sequentially** (runbook §1, read-merge-write race), `--bayesian-trials` ~300–500 or multi-criterion auto-stop (`bayesian_trials=None`). Per-trial cost is **nvcc/hipcc build-dominated** (megakernel cells slowest), plus a short on-device timing.

**Critical framing:** new live dims do **not** multiply the build count — they **dilute the fixed trial budget**, raising trials-to-converge by ~1.5–2×. This is the argument for adding dims sparingly.

- **sm_90**: 2 body archs total in the fleet, but sm_90 is the one with bodies. Adding the NOW dims (#1 MIN_BLOCKS SAFE, #2 reg-split SAFE) is cheap — SAFE dims need no parity re-run. Block-size dims (#3/#6/#7) and grad-tile (#5) each need a **parity-gate re-run** post-sweep. Estimated sweep: 11 opt × ~300–450 trials × (build≈seconds–minutes/cell) ≈ the existing per-opt budget × ~1.5–2 if the RISKY block dims are added; SAFE-only addition is near-free dilution.
- **gfx942**: only #8 (HIP mega block) + #10 (scan minBlocks) are real today; the 4 AMD dead dims stay pinned. Lower trial count (smaller live space). Same sequential 11-opt structure.
- **Pallas/TPU**: **do not add trials** until the kwargs are wired (else pure waste on identical configs).

**Recommended order:** (1) the two **SAFE** NOW rows (#1 `MIN_BLOCKS`, #2 prod/cons regs) — register + ship, no parity re-run, lowest risk/highest certainty. (2) the **RISKY** block/tile/grad rows (#3,5,6,7,8,9,11,12) — each requires the source guard edit (outside this scope) + a `parity_gate_h100.py` re-run after the sweep. (3) **R2 headers** — only after wgmma/tile_pipeline are `#include`d by a real compute TU. (4) **Pallas** — only after `pl.pallas_call` kwarg wiring.</result>

## Report: wgmma substrate audit, fix, and validation

**Outcome: all gates pass (18/18 pytest, end-to-end, sm_90a on the H100).** The substrate had three correctness bugs (two coupled, one independent) plus one broken test assertion; all fixed within the 4 assigned files. No commits, no forbidden files touched.

### Bugs found and fixed (primary sources: in-repo CUTLASS `cute`, which the design doc names as ground truth)

**1. Wrong smem operand layout + wrong descriptor LBO/SBO + wrong TransB (coupled — caused gates a–d to fail; A=I gave max_err=1.178).**
The ss-wgmma `.f32.bf16.bf16` K-major operand is NOT plain row-major. CUTLASS `make_gmma_desc&lt;Major::K&gt;` / `Layout_K_INTER_Atom` (verified by compiling a host probe against `third_party/cutlass`) require the canonical core-matrix layout: element `(mn,k)` at bf16 index `(k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)` — two stacked 8-wide core matrices. The descriptor fields must be **LBO = MN·16 bytes, SBO = 128 bytes** (the code had `lbo=16, sbo=256`). And both operands are Major-K (`Major::K==0`), so **TransB=0**, not 1 (the code had 1 → B was read with wrong major-ness, producing `D[m,n]=B[m,n]` instead of `Σ_k A[m,k]B[n,k]`).
Fixed in: `wgmma.cuh` (`make_desc_{A,B}_kmajor` → `&lt;MN,Swizzle&gt;(smem)` with correct LBO/SBO), `wgmma_selftest.cu` (canonical-layout staging scatter + TransB=0), `tile_pipeline.cuh` (canonical cp.async scatter + TransB=0).

**2. Pipeline deadlock (hung gates c/d before fix).** `elect_one_sync()` elects one leader **per warp**; the producer/consumer warpgroups are 4 warps each, so 4 threads arrived on barriers created with `init(1)` → phase flipped an even number of times → consumer's `try_wait.parity` missed the edge → infinite spin. Fixed in `tile_pipeline.cuh`: `init(128)` and **all 128 threads of each warpgroup arrive** (dropped the elect guard). This also closes a latent memory-visibility hole — each thread's `wgmma_wait_group&lt;0&gt;`/`cp_async_wait_group&lt;0&gt;` now happens-before its own arrive, so the phase-flip is ordered after every staged byte.

**3. SwizzleMode enum mismatch (latent; tested NONE-path unaffected).** Code had `32B=1, 128B=3`; CUTLASS `LayoutType` is `128B=1, 64B=2, 32B=3`. Corrected the enum + comments. NONE=0 agrees, so no gate was affected, but the perf-phase swizzle modes would have been wrong.

**4. Gate (f) asserted on PTX absent from the cubin (would FAIL on a correct kernel).** The test greps `cuobjdump -ptx`, but a `code=sm_90a`-only fatbin embeds no PTX (confirmed: empty output) → the wgmma.mma_async/commit/wait_group assertions were all 0. Fixed in the test: added `-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=compute_90a` so the fatbin carries PTX too (SASS execution unchanged).

### Per-gate results
- **(a) single-tile, fp64 reference of bf16-rounded inputs:** A=I localization max_err=**0.000e+00**; N∈{8,16,32,64,96,128} K=16 max_err **6e-7…1.7e-6**; ragged head 97→128 real_err **1.4e-6**, pad cols exactly 0.
- **(b) K-loop accumulation:** N=64/128 K=128 **8.0e-6 / 9.2e-6**; K=512 (ff2 depth) **5.9e-5**. Errors scale with K (the only residual is fp32 accumulation order over bf16-exact products), confirming the accumulation model.
- **(c) pipelined (depth 2 &amp; 3, N 64 &amp; 128):** **bit-identical** to unpipelined; vs-ref 7e-6…1.1e-5.
- **(d) determinism:** unpipelined A==A==A and pipelined P==P **bit-exact**.
- **(e) occupancy/refuse:** device cap 232448 B; 16 KB → occ 5; oversized → occ 0 (refuse) and oversized launch returns err_code 1 (cudaErrorInvalidValue), **no hang**.
- **(f) SASS/PTX audit:** HGMMA(SASS)=30, wgmma.mma_async(PTX)=20, commit_group=10, wait_group=10, setmaxnreg(PTX)=8, LDGSTS=10. bf16 wgmma is **not** FMA-lowered. Registers: `gemm_single_tile&lt;128&gt;` REG=90 **STACK=0 (no spill in the accumulator path)**; pipelined REG=58–90, STACK=8 (d2)/16 (d3). The 20 STL / 8 LDL spills live in the pipelined parity-array handling, **not** the wgmma loop.

### Tolerance derivation (stated)
fp32 accumulator over bf16-exact products: bf16 inputs are exact on both sides and each bf16×bf16 product is exact in fp32, so the **only** error source is fp32 summation order (hardware ascending-k vs the fp64 reference). Bound ≈ K·ε_fp32·max|partial|, ε_fp32=2^-24≈6e-8; for K≤512, unit-scale operands, that's a few e-4 worst case. Observed max ~6e-5 at K=512 sits well under the test's `atol=rtol=2e-3` floor. A ~1e-2 error would indicate a layout/transpose/TF32 bug, not bf16 noise — the test (correctly) does not loosen to absorb that. Reference is fp64-on-CPU with TF32 disabled (stricter than the asked fp32-of-bf16; fine).

### API contract a model-stage header consumes (all in `sg::sm90::wgs::`)
**The load-bearing trap (what bit the prior agent):** operands MUST be staged in the canonical Major-K core-matrix layout `idx(mn,k)=(k/8)*(MN*8)+mn*8+(k%8)`; plain row-major silently yields garbage with **no compile error**.
- `make_desc_A_kmajor&lt;M=64, Swizzle=kSwizzleNone&gt;(smem)` / `make_desc_B_kmajor&lt;N, Swizzle&gt;(smem)` — MN extent is now a compile-time template arg (was a runtime stride).
- `wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16&lt;N, ScaleD, TransA=0, TransB=0&gt;(acc, descA, descB)`; `WgmmaAccum&lt;N&gt;` (N/2 fp32 regs); `wgmma_frag_decode(tid,i,N,&amp;row,&amp;col)` for the epilogue (validated correct — A=I exact).
- `wgmma_mainloop_kchain&lt;N,0,0&gt;(acc, k_steps, gen)` (unpipelined) and `tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16&lt;N,Depth&gt;(gA,gB,gD,k_steps)` (turnkey pipelined) both assume **per-K-tile-contiguous global `[k_steps][MN][16]`**. A consumer whose activations are `[M,K]` adapts the source indexing; the smem/descriptor contract is unaffected.

### Honest caveats / deviations from the design doc
- **m64 is the validated unit.** `SG_TUNED_TILE_M=128` atom-stacking (TILE_M/64 stacked atoms) is the consumer's responsibility and is **not exercised** here.
- **N validated ≤128.** The header comment lists `{...,256}` but there is no N=256 overload or dispatcher case — N=256 is not callable as written.
- **Swizzle: only NONE is validated.** The 128B-swizzle layout (design §4.1 perf target) is enum-corrected but untested; it's a perf-phase item, not a correctness gate.
- **Pipeline is numerically correct but wgmma-serialized per iteration** (ptxas C7515: commit_group/wait_group every k-step). Gate (c) validates the mbarrier choreography + double/triple-buffering, **not** load/compute overlap. `setmaxnreg` is reported "ignored" by ptxas (C7508) in these standalone test kernels. # R2.3 — Fork-B decoder tensor-core cell driver: REPORT

The phase-restructured fwd+bwd+AdamW persistent megakernel is authored, builds, links, imports, runs real HGMMA on silicon, and passes every gate. The 1.8× speedup over the scalar L3-REAL path is validated at the same config it is gated for correctness.

## Deliverables (confined to the 4 named files)
- `csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh` — Fork-B engine + fwd/bwd tile drivers + dW/bias/embed/lnvec P2 helpers
- `csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh` (wgmma branch) — `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc&lt;Opt&gt;` 4-phase kernel + `launch_*_tc` (occupancy-certified, ncta_cap-capable)
- `csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc.cu` (new TU, `-DSG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL=1`) — `tc_train_step`, `tc_dump_ff2_operands` (ISO hook), `scalar_train_step` (matched-timing mirror)
- `tests/hw/test_decoder_tc.py` — PART2 full-cell gates

Build-only wiring confirmed: `setup.py:_collect` content-filters any `.cu` declaring `PYBIND11_MODULE(TORCH_EXTENSION_NAME` (line 433-445), so the TC TU is excluded from the main `_ops` build with **no glob change**; the gate JIT-loads it via `cpp_extension.load`. No commits.

## Gates — ALL PASS (clean single record: `/tmp/all_gates.out`, re-confirmed at nCTA=132 in `/tmp/all_gates_132.out`)
| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Single-step grad parity vs bf16-faithful fp64 oracle | worst **0.88× tol** @ layers.1.ff.0.bias (rel 7.02e-2, tol 0.08); layer-0 ≈ layer-1 uniform |
| dW GEMM ISO (own operands, incl. Kin=dff 4-N-tile path) | **3.338e-07** — bit-exact |
| Determinism A/A/A (grad + loss) | **bit-identical** |
| 50-step trajectory vs eager-bf16 | max rel-dev **3.69e-03**; kernel-only 4.8152 → 0.0281, no NaN/Inf |
| nCTA=2 (2 tiles/CTA, within-CTA cross-tile accum) | worst rel **9.81e-2** @ layers.1.ff.2.weight (&lt; 0.15) |
| **nCTA=132 (16 tiles → 116 idle CTAs in P1)** | **identical** to capped: parity 7.02e-2, ISO 3.338e-7, A/A/A, traj 3.69e-3 |
| PART1 GEMM orientations (fwd/dX/dW × all shapes) | all OK, dW determinism bit-identical |

## Step-time: scalar vs TC (the perf milestone)
Both paths, **same cell, nCTA=132, back-to-back, one process, identical live-fleet contention**:
- **SCALAR 12053.3 µs/step**, **TC 6690.2 µs/step** → **ratio 1.80× (TC faster)**.

Honesty notes: absolute µs are contention-rough (quiet-GPU absolute is a follow-up). The earlier **23952µs@nCTA=4 was a memory-crunch artifact, discarded.** At B=512 the fwd/bwd is **tile-limited to 16 active CTAs** of 132 (the other 116 work only in the dW phase) — so TC beats scalar 1.8× *despite* filling 16/132 SMs in fwd/bwd; a larger batch (more tiles) would raise TC's fwd/bwd utilization further.

## SASS / resources (fresh from the rebuilt `.so`)
- **REG 251, STACK 1152 B, LOCAL 0 (zero spills), SHARED 8628 B, CONST 792 B**, occupancy ≥ 1.
- **18× HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16** — the real bf16/fp32-acc warpgroup MMAs (write real registers): 8 fwd (4/layer×2) + 8 dX (4/layer×2) + 9 dW... materialized as 18 static issue points in the unpipelined engine; head/CE/attention/LN are scalar fp32 (M=nsamp=32 &lt; the wgmma m64 floor).
- **9× HGMMA.64x8x16.F16** — **all operands are RZ (zero in, bit-bucket out), all 9 byte-identical** → inert. No fp16 exists anywhere in the source (verified). ISO 3.3e-7 + the trajectory confirm zero functional/precision effect.
- ptxas **C7515** serialization remark present — the SASS-level confirmation of the unpipelined (0-LDGSTS) engine deviation below.

## Deviations from the Fork-B contract
1. **Unpipelined engine** (`tc_gemm_block_unpipelined`, 0 async LDGSTS) — staging is synchronous; C7515 is its SASS signature. Correct, not maximally overlapped.
2. **AdamW not fused into the dW epilogue** — runs as a separate **P3** scalar optimizer tail after B2. Phase structure is **3 grid barriers** (B0 zero-lnvec / B1 acts-complete / B2 grad-ready+reset) + P3, not the single-epilogue-fusion the contract sketched. Fork-B's "no B1 partial-reduce barrier" *is* honored (no cross-CTA dW reduction); B1 here is an acts-completion fence.
3. **Weights bf16-on-read** (`__float2bfloat16(W[...])` in the GEMM accessors) — params stay fp32 in HBM; no separate bf16 weight buffer.
4. **kSwizzleNone** in the smem staging (no XOR swizzle).
5. **Per-CTA + per-layer fp32 tile scratch** (the per-layer-array cache fix) — workspace ≈ **222 MB at nCTA=132** (≈ the scalar path's 223 MB; the 1.5 MB/CTA scratch is the dominant term, NOT the launch limiter — earlier nCTA caps were over-conservative).
6. **ncta_cap test affordance** on the launcher (shipped path passes 0 = full saturation).

## ViT / Mamba port deltas
- **ViT** (`model_stage_vit.cuh`: kSeq=17, kPatch=49, kHeads=4, kD=128, kLayers=2, kDff=512, kVocab=97): (a) **full bidirectional attention, no causal mask**; (b) **patch-projection** Linear(49→128) replaces the embedding lookup (a new fwd wgmma + its dX/dW); (c) **CLS-token head** reads position-0, not last; (d) **kSeq=17 ⇒ `kTileM` must be a multiple of 17** (vs 4) — re-tiling and a different sample↔tile-boundary alignment. Attention/LN/GELU/CE stay scalar fp32 as in the decoder.
- **Mamba** (`model_stage_mamba3.cuh`: kSeq=8, d_inner=256, state_dim=16, dt_rank=8, conv_k=3): the **selective scan stays a scalar register-resident recurrence** (h[seq][d_inner][state] ≈128 KB/sample cannot fit smem — unrolled t=0..7 in registers, fwd+reverse-time bwd). **Only the projection GEMMs** (in_proj, x_proj, dt_proj, out_proj) go wgmma; the scan and the depthwise causal conv remain scalar. No attention block at all.</result>

## Report: Decoder TC forward bias fix + gate tightening

### The bug (confirmed and fixed)
`csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh` — `dectc_forward_tile` omitted four linear biases that the scalar decoder and the bf16-faithful oracle both apply: `in_proj` (`in_b`), `out_proj` (`out_b`), `ff0` (`ff0_b`), `ff2` (`ff2_b`). Only the head `out_b` and the LN betas were present. The omission was masked at init by the 0.15 grad tolerance.

### The fix (4 spots, ViT bias-epilogue pattern, matching the oracle's precision boundary)
- **qkv**: after the GEMM, fold `in_b` in fp32 and re-round to bf16 (mirrors ViT exactly; double-round is idempotent at init where `in_b=0`).
- **out_proj `a`**: add `out_b` in the fp32 `r1 = Xin + a + out_b` step.
- **ff0**: add `ff0_b` to the fp32 `pre` before storing `ff0pre` and computing GELU.
- **ff2**: add `ff2_b` in the fp32 `r2 = x1 + ff2 + ff2_b` step.

Backward / P2 dW / bias code untouched — `db = Σ_t dY` is independent of the bias value and was already structurally correct. The DATAFLOW header comment was updated to record the folds.

### Gates — before vs after (full suite, bare, `CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/nonexistent`, `SG_TC_NCTA_CAP=8`)

| Metric | Before (buggy) | After (fixed) |
|---|---|---|
| **loss rel** | 2.52e-04 | **2.85e-05** (~9x tighter) |
| **worst grad ratio** | 0.88× tol (ff.0.bias) | **0.06× tol** (ff.0.bias) |
| worst weight-grad rel | 9.81e-02 (ff.2.w) | ~7.1e-03 (in_proj.w) |
| k-vs-bf16 grads | well above floor | **≈ bf16-vs-fp64 floor (6.07e-03)** |
| dW-isolation (own operands) | — | 2.77e-07 (bit-exact) |
| 50-step trajectory rel-dev | — | 2.50e-03 (gate 0.15) |

**Full suite: 18 passed, 0 failed.** Grad gates left at 0.15/0.08 (the documented dW T-contraction bf16 floor, pinned by the GEMM-exact isolation test — not loosened).

### Gate tightening (no-suppression)
`_TC_LOSS_REL` tightened 5e-3 → **1e-4** in `tests/hw/test_decoder_tc.py`. Calibrated to the measured (2.85e-5 fixed, 2.52e-4 buggy) window, geometric-mean-centered: passes the faithful kernel with 3.5x headroom and **catches the bias bug with 2.5x margin** (the buggy 2.52e-4 &gt; 1e-4). A two-TU link probe surfaced the real blocker: 5 non-template `__device__` helpers in `model_stages_decoder.cuh` (and 5 in `model_stage_vit.cuh`) collided at host link when a second TU included them. Fixed by marking them `inline` (vague linkage; `__forceinline__` avoided for the large ones) — the correct latent-ODR fix, not a workaround. ## TC-Conversion Cycle 2 — Report

**Converted this cycle: +5 cells → 9/33 (27.3%) on L3-TC wgmma (3/11 per model).** Baseline was 4 (decoder/vit×{adamw,lion}; mamba×adamw ran L3-*scalar*, not wgmma). All gates green: tail gate 9/9, wiring_check 9/33 on the production race path, roofline 33 rows @ B=16384 + png — and the roofline JSON independently confirms all 9 converted cells at `l3_engine='wgmma'`, `l3_steps_fired=155` (no eager leakage).

Mapped to the cited blockers:

- **(a) grokfast — CONVERTED ×3 models (decoder/vit/mamba), end-to-end.** Root cause was the ema cold-start: eager seeds `ema=grad0` (grokfast.py `_group_cache`), the kernel zero-inits ema. Fixed in `apply_optimizer&lt;Grokfast&gt;` (opt_components.cuh): at `step==1`, `st.ema[idx]=grad[idx]` → `e_new=α·g+(1−α)·g=g` matches eager exactly. **Observed ema state rel 0.98 → 0.000** in the tail gate. Wired the Python gates + `train_grokfast` (mirrors `train_lion`). grokfast has no grad_clip and `_opt_scalars_from` already forwards α/λ, so cold-start was the only gap.

- **(b) grokadamw — BLOCKED (deferred). Directive scope was incomplete.** Item (b) specified only the per-tensor β1 side-channel; I found **three** mechanisms all required: (i) per-tensor layer-wise β1=β1·(1−γ)^layer — a HARD step-1 state-gate fail, **observed m-rel 0.895** (temp-registered, ran gate, reverted); (ii) per-tensor grad-norm clip to 1.0 (eager `clip_grad_norms_device_side`; **measured inert at step 1 / fires by step 50**, param rel 2e-4); (iii) adaptive α_t. The ema cold-start is staged in the kernel; remaining gap is exactly (i)+(ii)+(iii). Building only the side-channel would pass the step-1 gate while diverging multi-step — a hollow pass the no-suppression rule forbids, so the whole cell stays blocked.

- **(c) mamba — launcher WIRED; converted ×3 of 4 requested (adamw/lion/grokfast).** Built `mega_mamba_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu` (in-_ops, OptId-generic, mirrors decoder/vit) + dispatch.cpp wgmma branch + extern decl. Hit a real ODR link bug: mamba's scalar scan/conv helpers (`mb_layernorm_bwd`, `mb_scan_fwd`, …) were external-linkage `__device__` (vs decoder's `__device__ inline`) — two TUs including them clashed. Fixed by making the 8 helpers `inline` (linkage-only, matches decoder pattern; scalar regression loss 4.75274 ✓, **test_mamba_tc 5/5 grad-vs-oracle ✓**). mamba×grokadamw excluded for (b)'s reasons.

- **(d) neuralgrok — KERNEL-READY, RACE-BLOCKED.** The psi MLP is already in opt_components.cuh and `kPsiHidden=16` matches the race's `neural_hidden=16` (2-layer), so snapshot-plumbing would pass the tail gate (and grad_clip is **inert at steps 1&amp;50, max grad-norm 0.72&lt;1.0**). But the real blocker is the race integration: `train_neuralgrok` trains the amplifier between steps via a differentiable Python rebuild needing model grads, while the L3 megakernel returns only loss — snapshot alone yields a frozen (non-faithful) amplifier. ## Summary

Implemented INTEGRATION-NOTES.md §1–§2 fully: the SuperGrok2 full CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta-net persistent megakernel (`opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh`) is now wired, callable, and parity-validated against the per-op oracle on a real H100.

### What was done (4 files; header untouched)

1. **`csrc/fused/sm_90/sg2_meta_tail.cu`** (NEW TU) — the §1b host-wrapper bodies. `bindings.cpp` is host-only `.cpp` and cannot `#include` the `.cuh` (host gcc can't parse `kernel&lt;&lt;&lt;...&gt;&gt;&gt;`), so the marshalling lives here where nvcc compiles it. Defines `sg::sg2_meta_optimizer_tail(...)` (marshals packed buffers + fp32 meta bundle + scalars into `SG2Weights`/`SG2State`/`SG2Scalars`/`PersistentContext`, launches the templated `launch_sg2_meta_optimizer_tail&lt;SG2Dims&lt;&gt;,float,float&gt;`) and `sg::sg2_ws_stride(int64_t)` (exposes the authoritative `sg2_ws_stride&lt;SG2Dims&lt;&gt;&gt;`). Owns no `PYBIND11_MODULE`, so setup.py's `csrc/fused/sm_90/*.cu` glob links it into `_ops` and the content-filter doesn't drop it — no setup.py edit needed.

2. **`csrc/bindings/bindings.cpp`** — extern decls + the two `m.def` registrations (`sg2_meta_optimizer_tail` with the full §1a `py::arg` list, `sg2_ws_stride`). Purely additive; the existing `supergrok2_batched_step` oracle path is unchanged.

3. **`grokking_optimizers/optimizers/supergrok2.py`** — `SuperGrok2.sg2_step_megakernel(params, grads, sharpness_list, states, meta, scalars)` per §2: packs all tensors back-to-back, computes per-tensor `perm`/`unsort` via the exact `|grad|.sort(descending=False)` the oracle uses, sizes the workspace from the `sg2_ws_stride` binding (no drift), calls the op, unpacks in place.

4. **`tests/hw/test_sg2_megakernel.py`** — filled the (B1)/(B2) skip bodies. Both drive the ops directly from one identical (weights, state, scalar-vectors) set — oracle = `supergrok2_batched_step`, megakernel = `sg2_step_megakernel` — on cloned buffers. Continuous randn grads (no `|grad|` ties → the two independent sorts coincide). Scalar map matches `csa_hca_step_one`: `gru_decay←beta1`, `alpha←alpha_mu`, `lamb_eff←lamb_effs`.

### Parity numbers (real H100, tol 1e-5)

**B1 single-step** (sizes 5/17/64/200/1/333, 2 seeds; N=333 exercises the low-rank CSA indexer at 16-of-84):
- max|Δparam| 4.66e-10 / 2.91e-11, max|Δexp_avg| ≤1.94e-07, max|Δexp_avg_sq| ≤1.49e-08
- max|Δmu| 1.13e-06 / **2.16e-06** (worst), max|Δslow| **0** (exact), max|Δgru_state| ≤8.94e-08

**B2 200-step trajectory** (evolving bias-correction `t=step+1`): worst per-step max|Δparam| 2.38e-07, worst Δmean|param| 5.96e-08, final max|Δparam| 2.38e-07, final **max|Δmu| 2.22e-06**, final max|Δslow| 0.

Two different meanings of "maxed," and only one is true:

1. **Maxed against the levers we've found** — mostly yes, and still improving. The wins are real and large *relative to where they started*: mamba 0.46×→2.15× vs scalar, vit +3.48×, structural bugs (serialization, redundant reductions, spills) fixed. The loop keeps finding more.

These grokking models are *tiny* — d=128, seq 4–17, ~0.4M params, ~45 µs of actual math per step. The arithmetic intensity is so low that the roofline ceiling *at that intensity* (min(compute, AI·bandwidth)) is the bandwidth slope, not the 989 TF/s flat peak — and you can't manufacture arithmetic that isn't in a 0.4M-param model. A perfectly-written kernel here still lands single-digit-percent of peak.

So the honest state: each cell is being driven to the best version *its shape allows*, the relative speedups are genuine and worth having (faster race, real engineering story), but the **bars will stay low in absolute terms** — that's physics of small models, not headroom we're leaving on the table.

The only way to make the bars approach 100% is to change the experiment (bigger models / batched problem), which would change what you're measuring. Within the grokking race as specified, "maxed" means "best version of each small kernel," which is what the swarm is producing — not "near the flat compute peak," which is unreachable here. ## Summary

**Root cause:** `train_neuralgrok` in `grokking_race_v2.py` never called `_try_fused_train_step` — it went straight to the eager forward/backward/`opt.step()` path. The `neuralgrok×{decoder,vit,mamba}` cells were correctly registered in `_FUSED_L3_REAL` and `_L3_WGMMA_CELLS` (so dispatch said ENABLED and `gemm_impl_for_cell` returned `wgmma`), but with no hook in the train loop, `LAST_L3_ENGINE` stayed `None` every step. The WIRING-GUARD (`_record_train_path` in grokking_race_v2.py:778) correctly detected this and emitted "expected L3-TC bf16 but ran eager — L3-REAL path did NOT fire (not ABI-stale)." So the task's second hypothesis was right: the function never called it.

**The fix** (the genuinely subtle part): unlike adamw/lion, neuralgrok trains an amplifier MLP whose lookahead autograd can't run in-kernel. The codebase already had the documented seam — `NeuralGrok.maybe_train_amplifier`/`train_amplifier_step` (needs host `p.grad` for the `|g|` featurization). So I kept the existing host fwd+bwd+amplifier-train prefix verbatim, then called `_try_fused_train_step("neuralgrok",...)` and skipped the eager `scaler.step(opt)` on a fused hit (mirroring `train_adamw`'s L3 branch). The kernel computes its own TC-reduced grad and owns the weight update; the host backward is amplifier featurization only; `fused_train_step` scatters the freshly-trained `psi_pack()` into the kernel's `extra` slice before the launch. Amplifier trains every step — no suppression.

**dispatch.py** needed no logic change (everything was already wired); I corrected only a stale comment (lines 708-709) that claimed mamba×neuralgrok was OUT — it's wired via the wave-2 mamba lane and now empirically confirmed.

**Validation on a fresh `FORCE_CUDA=1 ./build.sh`:**
- **wiring_check** `--opts neuralgrok` → 3/3 = `L3-TC-megakernel(wgmma)` (100%). The proving line:
  `[PASS L3-TC] neuralgrok /decoder  path=L3-TC-megakernel(wgmma)` (plus vit and mamba identically)
- **tail_gate** `-k neuralgrok` → 3 passed, run 3 separate times (A/A/A), bit-identical: (1a) params vs eager rel ~1e-7, (1b) state vs canonical neuralgrok.h ~1e-6, determinism loss/grad/param-eq across all 3.
- **No-suppression verified empirically** (the gap neither gate covers, since `_component_guard` swallows exceptions): 0 component/amplifier failures across the routed wiring_check run, plus a direct test showing all 4 amplifier weight tensors move after one `train_amplifier_step` (max|delta|=1e-3).

**Committed** as `b57a08e` on branch `claude/h100-audit-maximal`: `grokking_race_v2.py` (+22), `grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py` (comment fix, ±4), and the green `wiring_check.json` proof. Unrelated working-tree changes (build.log, roofline.json/png from prior work) were left out of the commit.
